conclusion: Subtrial A requires a hybrid InteractiveExperiences rebuild. Replace lifted DirectManipulation with the system runtime; rebuild Input, InputStateManager, and Windowing Core against system Composition, DispatcherQueue, and CoreMessaging; then retain their three public facade dependents against the rebuilt Windowing Core ABI.

runtimeModules.name: Microsoft.DirectManipulation.dll
runtimeModules.reason: The lifted runtime directly and transitively reaches dcompi, CoreMessagingXP, lifted Composition support, marshal, dwmcorei, and wuceffectsi.

runtimeModules.name: Microsoft.UI.Input.dll
runtimeModules.replacement: Hybrid IXP binary using system Composition, CoreMessaging, DispatcherQueue, and system input/content primitives
runtimeModules.reason: This binary owns the lifted Input and Content activation surface and directly imports forbidden Composition and CoreMessaging support.

runtimeModules.name: Microsoft.InputStateManager.dll
runtimeModules.replacement: Hybrid IXP binary using system Composition and CoreMessaging
runtimeModules.reason: The input state implementation shares the forbidden lifted Composition and CoreMessaging dependency chain with Microsoft.UI.Input.dll.

runtimeModules.name: Microsoft.UI.Windowing.Core.dll
runtimeModules.replacement: Hybrid IXP binary using system CoreMessaging and DispatcherQueue
runtimeModules.reason: Windowing Core directly imports CoreMessagingXP and is the common dependency of the retained Windowing, Graphics.Display, and Microsoft.UI facades.

runtimeModules.name: Microsoft.UI.Windowing.dll
runtimeModules.replacement: Retain against the ABI-compatible rebuilt Microsoft.UI.Windowing.Core.dll
runtimeModules.reason: It has no direct forbidden import; its only forbidden reachability is through Windowing Core.

runtimeModules.name: Microsoft.Graphics.Display.dll
runtimeModules.replacement: Retain against the ABI-compatible rebuilt Microsoft.UI.Windowing.Core.dll
runtimeModules.reason: It has no direct forbidden import; its only forbidden reachability is through Windowing Core.

runtimeModules.name: Microsoft.UI.dll
runtimeModules.replacement: Retain against the ABI-compatible rebuilt Microsoft.UI.Windowing.Core.dll while XAML public common types are evaluated separately
runtimeModules.reason: It has no direct forbidden import; its only forbidden reachability is through Windowing Core.

families.windows11: Windows.UI.WindowId is available in the GE system IDL; Colors and ColorHelper are system XAML/UI surfaces.
families.windows10: Windows.UI.WindowId is absent. The intentional API break is accepted for Windows 10.

families.windows11: System input supplies the underlying implementation primitives, but only a small subset is shape-compatible with the lifted public API.
families.windows10: System input exists but lacks later island/input-object functionality and is not a public one-to-one replacement.

families.windows11: System primitives can host the implementation, but ContentIsland and site-bridge contracts have no public one-to-one system replacement.
families.windows10: The available system content/island surface differs further and cannot preserve the lifted API shape.

families.windows11: The system WindowManagement API is not shape- or behavior-equivalent to Microsoft.UI.Windowing.
families.windows10: Windows.UI.WindowManagement exists, but the same incompatibility remains.

families.windows11: System and lifted builds share source partitions; switch WinUI to the system runtime and validate every lifted extension used by XAML.
families.windows10: The system runtime exists, but later lifted extensions may be unavailable and require accepted feature loss.

families.windows11: Use the system DispatcherQueue/CoreMessaging implementation and rebuild dependent IXP binaries to remove CoreMessagingXP imports.
families.windows10: Basic system DispatcherQueue is available; lifted lifecycle extensions require WinUI-owned replacement logic.
